questions.question: How do you want to get into melnick's shares to search for Mint exports?

options.label: You mount in Finder, I search
options.description: Cmd-K → smb://melnick.local, pick the share that holds the archive. Once it's at /Volumes/<share>, I'll grep for mint/intuit/transactions exports.

options.label: Tell me share + creds, I mount
options.description: Give me the share name (e.g. "archive", "home") and the username (DSM creds). I'll mount it from CLI — password via macOS auth prompt, not in chat.

options.label: Search Time Machine backup instead
options.description: Skip melnick shares — use the already-mounted Mac mini Time Machine and look for Mint exports there (slower; sparsebundle).

options.label: Skip — just wait for the Intuit download
options.description: Don't dig into melnick; proceed once the fresh Intuit export arrives.

transcript_tail.text:
No volume named "Melnick" is currently mounted. The mounted volumes right now are:

- `Backups of Daniel's Mac mini` (Time Machine)
- `Macintosh HD`
- `Obsidian 1.12.7-universal` (installer DMG)

Plug in the Melnick drive and I'll search it once it shows up under `/Volumes/`. If you want, I can also peek into the Time Machine backup for any Mint exports the Mac mini might have had — just say the word.
That's a Synology NAS web UI (DSM on port 5001). I can't log into the web UI, but I can mount/search it from the filesystem side.
Confirmed — NAS is named `melnick.local` (so voice transcription was actually accurate, not a mishear). Time Machine already auto-mounts one share. Let me see what shares it exposes.
SMB needs auth. Before asking for credentials, checking if there's a saved share or recent connection I can use.
Saving what I've learned about `melnick` for future sessions.
